use_cases.label: Build your first app
use_cases.question: I have an idea and no dev setup. What do I use?

tools.name: Lovable
tools.line: Turns a plain-English description into a styled web app, with a database and GitHub sync available.
tools.use: You want something that looks finished on the first try.
tools.skip: You need fine control over how the code is organized.

tools.name: Replit
tools.line: Builds, runs and hosts the app in one browser tab, so there is nothing to install.
tools.use: You want it live on the internet today.
tools.skip: You plan to move the project into your own tooling soon.

tools.name: Bolt
tools.line: Runs the whole dev environment in the browser, which makes it quick for throwaway prototypes.
tools.use: You are testing an idea before committing to it.
tools.skip: You need a long-lived app with real users.

tools.name: v0
tools.line: Generates interface screens and components that deploy on Vercel.
tools.use: The hard part of your idea is the interface, not the logic.
tools.skip: You want a full backend generated for you.

use_cases.label: Ship real software
use_cases.question: I can code and want an AI pair that handles real projects.

tools.name: Cursor
tools.line: A code editor built around AI: autocomplete, chat over your codebase, and agents that edit many files.
tools.use: You live in an editor and want the AI inside it.
tools.skip: You would rather hand off whole tasks and review the result.

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.line: A terminal agent that reads your project, makes changes across files and runs your tests.
tools.use: You want to delegate a whole task and review the diff.
tools.skip: You prefer to stay in a graphical editor all day.
tools.note: Disclosure: made by Anthropic, whose Claude models also run Loadout's agents.

tools.name: GitHub Copilot
tools.line: Suggestions and chat inside the editors and GitHub workflow many teams already use.
tools.use: Your team is on GitHub and wants a low-friction rollout.
tools.skip: You want the most autonomous agent available.

tools.name: Codex
tools.line: OpenAI's coding agent for handing off software tasks.
tools.use: You already work in OpenAI's tools.
tools.skip: You need an editor-first workflow.

use_cases.label: Build AI agents
use_cases.question: I want an agent that does a job on its own. Where do I build it?

tools.name: n8n
tools.line: A visual workflow builder with AI agent steps, and it can be self-hosted.
tools.use: You want agents wired to real apps without writing a framework.
tools.skip: You need fine-grained control over agent state.

tools.name: LangGraph
tools.line: A code framework for agents that need branching, loops and saved state.
tools.use: You are a developer building an agent for production.
tools.skip: You want a result this afternoon without writing code.

tools.name: CrewAI
tools.line: A framework for teams of role-based agents that hand work to each other.
tools.use: Your task splits cleanly into roles.
tools.skip: One agent with good tools would do the job.

tools.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
tools.line: A lightweight Python SDK for agents with tools, handoffs and guardrails.
tools.use: You build on OpenAI models.
tools.skip: You want a visual builder.

tools.name: Claude Agent SDK
tools.line: The agent loop behind Claude Code, packaged for your own agents.
tools.use: You want a ready-made loop for coding or task agents.
tools.skip: You want a no-code builder.
tools.note: Disclosure: made by Anthropic, whose Claude models also run Loadout's agents.

use_cases.label: Research and learn
use_cases.question: I need answers I can check, fast.

tools.name: Perplexity
tools.line: Gives answers with numbered links to the sources, aimed at quick lookups.
tools.use: You need a cited answer in under a minute.
tools.skip: You need a long report that merges many sources.

tools.name: NotebookLM
tools.line: Answers from the documents you upload, with citations back to them.
tools.use: You are studying a fixed pile of papers or notes.
tools.skip: You need fresh results from the open web.

tools.name: ChatGPT deep research
tools.line: Runs a multi-step web investigation and returns a long report with citations.
tools.use: You want a first draft of a literature scan.
tools.skip: You will not read the sources behind the claims.

tools.name: Gemini deep research
tools.line: Plans a multi-step web investigation and returns a cited report.
tools.use: You already live in Google's apps.
tools.skip: You will not read the sources behind the claims.

use_cases.label: Make games and assets
use_cases.question: I am building a game and need art, models and a faster prototype.

tools.name: Scenario
tools.line: Generates game art in a consistent style you train on your own assets.
tools.use: You need many assets that match one look.
tools.skip: You want a quick one-off concept image.

tools.name: Meshy
tools.line: Turns text or an image into a 3D model you can bring into an engine.
tools.use: You need placeholder or background props quickly.
tools.skip: You need animation-ready hero characters.

tools.name: Unity AI
tools.line: In February 2026 Unity announced an upgraded AI assistant that builds games from natural-language descriptions, with a beta planned for March. Check its current status before relying on it.
tools.use: You already build in Unity.
tools.skip: You need a stable, finished feature today.

tools.name: Midjourney
tools.line: Image generation suited to concept art and mood boards.
tools.use: You are exploring the look and feel of a game.
tools.skip: You need assets that match each other exactly.

use_cases.label: Make video and voice
use_cases.question: I want clips, trailers or narration without a studio.

tools.name: Runway
tools.line: Video generation and editing tools aimed at working creators.
tools.use: You want control over shots and edits, not only a prompt.
tools.skip: You want a finished film from a single prompt.

tools.name: Veo
tools.line: Google's video generation model family.
tools.use: You already work in Google's tools.
tools.skip: You want hands-on editing controls.

tools.name: Kling
tools.line: Generates video from text or an image.
tools.use: You want a second model to compare on the same prompt.
tools.skip: Where the vendor is based matters for your project.

tools.name: ElevenLabs
tools.line: Text to speech and voice tools.
tools.use: You need narration or character voices.
tools.skip: You need video.

drops.name: Gemini 4 Argon
drops.line: A model released for long-running agent workflows, available through the Gemini API, AI Studio and the Gemini platform.

drops.name: Gemini app task mode
drops.line: Lets the Gemini assistant keep working while you are away, with connections to more than 40 apps.

drops.name: Dots
drops.line: Always-on agents that pursue goals you set between conversations, starting with Pro and Business Premium customers.

drops.name: Hermes for Businesses
drops.line: An enterprise offering built on the open-source Hermes agent, deployable in Slack, Telegram, WhatsApp and other channels.

drops.name: Claude Haiku 5.5
drops.line: A fast, low-cost small model with a 1M-token context window, aimed at high-volume tasks. Anthropic also makes Claude Code, ranked on this site.

drops.name: Kimi K2.6
drops.line: An open-source model whose agent swarms can coordinate up to 1,000 agents on complex tasks.

drops.name: Autopilot
drops.line: A long-running agent that can work for days in a cloud sandbox with externalized memory.

drops.name: Agent Droplets
drops.line: A bundled monthly plan (Pro $50, Team $200) covering agent runtimes, inference, memory and governed tool access.

drops.name: Strands Decider 2B
drops.line: An open-source 2-billion-parameter decision model designed to run locally with confidence-scored outputs.

criteria.name: Result quality
criteria.how: Same task on every tool, judged against a fixed checklist.

criteria.name: Reliability
criteria.how: Does it hold up across repeat runs of the same task?

criteria.name: Cost for what you get
criteria.how: Price at the tier a normal user needs, against the result.

criteria.name: Time to first result
criteria.how: Minutes from sign-up to something usable.

criteria.name: Pace of improvement
criteria.how: How often it ships changes that matter.

patch_notes.text: Launch draft. Six jobs, four or five tools each. Picks are editorial, based on public information. No tool has been through the test harness yet, and the game-making list is the thinnest.
Build the test harness, run one fixed task per job on every listed tool, and replace editorial picks with scored ones. Each re-ranking will be logged here with the reason.
